findings.key_quote: Three Months Ended September 30, 2026 Compared with Three Months Ended September 30, 2025 Agents and Infra Revenue increased $15.1 billion or 25%. • Azure revenue increased $10.8 billion or 48% driven by demand for services across the platform
findings.justification: E1 has period_status EXACT_MATCH for the three months ended September 30, 2026. The passage states that Agents and Infra (which is the new name for Intelligent Cloud segment per E8) revenue increased $15.1 billion or 25%, and that Azure revenue increased $10.8 billion or 48%. Since Azure's increase of $10.8 billion represents the majority of the total segment revenue increase of $15.1 billion (71% of the total increase), this arithmetically demonstrates that Azure and other cloud services was the primary driver of the segment's revenue growth in the quarter.

findings.key_quote: Beginning in fiscal year 2027, the information that our chief operating decision maker is regularly provided and reviews for purposes of allocating resources and assessing performance reflects these segment changes. Prior period segment information has been recast
findings.justification: E8 provides context that the Agents and Infra segment is the renamed/restructured version of what was previously Intelligent Cloud, with changes effective in fiscal year 2027 (which includes the quarter ended September 30, 2026). This is relevant context for understanding the segment naming but does not itself decide whether Azure drove the growth.

findings.key_quote: Three Months Ended March 31, 2026 Compared with Three Months Ended March 31, 2025 Revenue increased $12.8 billion or 18% driven by growth in Microsoft Cloud. Intelligent Cloud revenue increased driven by Azure.
findings.justification: E2 has period_status MISMATCH (quarter ended March 31, 2026, not September 30, 2026). While it states that Intelligent Cloud revenue increased driven by Azure, this is for a different quarter and therefore does not decide the claim about the September 30, 2026 quarter.

findings.key_quote: Fiscal Year 2026 Compared with Fiscal Year 2025 Revenue increased $50.1 billion or 18% driven by growth in Microsoft Cloud. Intelligent Cloud revenue increased driven by Azure.
findings.justification: E3 has period_status MISMATCH (fiscal year 2026 ended June 30, 2026, not the quarter ended September 30, 2026). While it states Intelligent Cloud revenue increased driven by Azure, this is for a different 12-month period and does not decide the claim about the specific quarter.

findings.key_quote: Intelligent Cloud Revenue increased $31.5 billion or 30%. • Server products and cloud services revenue increased $31.0 billion or 31% driven by Azure and other cloud services. Azure and other cloud services revenue grew 41%
findings.justification: E4 has period_status MISMATCH (fiscal year ended June 30, 2026, not the quarter ended September 30, 2026). While it shows Azure and other cloud services drove Intelligent Cloud revenue growth, this is for a different 12-month period and does not decide the claim about the September 30, 2026 quarter.

findings.key_quote: Nine Months Ended March 31, 2026 Compared with Nine Months Ended March 31, 2025 Revenue increased $36.5 billion or 18% driven by growth in Microsoft Cloud. Intelligent Cloud revenue increased driven by Azure.
findings.justification: E5 has period_status MISMATCH (nine months ended March 31, 2026, not the three months ended September 30, 2026). While it states Intelligent Cloud revenue increased driven by Azure, this is for a different duration and period and does not decide the claim about the specific quarter.
